Hi Alice — thanks for the list. Below is a compact runbook with the options we support and what you should expect for an audit. TL;DR: we can do either tenant-managed CA or Redwood-managed termination; each has tradeoffs around key custody, OCSP availability, and rotation complexity.

1) Tenant-managed CA (you generate CSR/private key)
- Process: You create CSR(s) (we provide CSR template) and upload the CSR to the Redwood private control plane. Redwood returns the signed cert bundle (signed by your intermediate or root) for installation into our private runtime or a sidecar.
- Pros: You retain key custody (audit-friendly), easy to align with internal PKI policy.
- Cons: Requires a mechanism for cert refresh (automation recommended); if your CA is offline we can accept signed certs on a cadence but that increases manual steps.
- OCSP/CRL: If your CA uses OCSP and the clients have no egress, you must provide an internal OCSP responder or we can package proof-of-revocation via periodic CRL snapshots.

2) Redwood-managed TLS termination (proxy edge in your VPC)
- Process: Redwood provisions and manages certificates for the termination point running inside your VPC (we either use our ACME sidecar or a short-lived intermediate). Private keys are generated and stored in our ephemeral HSM in the customer's VPC.
- Pros: Minimal operator burden for your team, automatic rotation and OCSP stapling controlled by Redwood.
- Cons: Key custody is shared (we can provide audit logs / KMS proof). For high-compliance customers we offer an HSM-backed deployment in your project.

3) Mutual TLS (mTLS) for client authentication
- Patterns: client cert pinning (per-client certs) or SPIFFE-style workload identity. For S2S traffic we recommend mTLS with short-lived client certs issued by your internal CA, distributed via your secrets manager.

Rotation and availability
- Hot-swap: Certs can be hot-swapped in the runtime without downtime if the client and server support immediate reloads. We recommend canary rollout to 1-2 hosts before cluster-wide swap.
- Fallback: Redwood supports automatic fallback to a compatible model/proxy config for 60s during rotation.

Attached: CSR template (csr-template.pem) and a minimal on-prem diagram showing where the termination point lives. I'll loop Jordan for the openssl snippets and an example ACME sidecar command.

Action items
- Alice: confirm whether you require tenant key custody or if Redwood-managed is acceptable for this workload.
- FinTech SecOps: if tenant-managed, share PKI profile (validity, SANs, required OIDs).
- Redwood: we'll prepare a short PoC (1–2 hosts) to demonstrate hot-swap.

Best,

Hi Alice — Jordan here (Solutions Engineering). Quick technical addendum and sample commands you can include in the PoC so your ops team can validate automation: 

1) CSR template example (fields we expect)
- Subject: CN=proxy.vpc.internal.fintech-inc.local
- SANs: DNS:proxy.vpc.internal.fintech-inc.local, DNS:*.vpc.internal.fintech-inc.local, IP:10.32.7.12 (if you need IP SANs)
- Key: RSA 2048 or ECC P-256 acceptable; we recommend ECDSA for performance.

openssl req -new -newkey ec:<(openssl ecparam -name prime256v1) -nodes -keyout proxy.key -out proxy.csr -subj "\/CN=proxy.vpc.internal.fintech-inc.local" -reqexts SAN -config <(cat /etc/ssl/openssl.cnf 
[req]
default_bits = 2048
prompt = no
req_extensions = SAN
[ SAN ]
subjectAltName = @alt_names
[ alt_names ]
DNS.1 = proxy.vpc.internal.fintech-inc.local
DNS.2 = *.vpc.internal.fintech-inc.local
IP.1 = 10.32.7.12)

2) OCSP / CRL and offline environments
- If the OCSP responder is unreachable, the behavior depends on client policy. Redwood can configure the proxy to fail-open (accept certs when revocation check fails) or fail-closed. For high-security workloads we default to fail-closed; this is configurable per-customer.
- For fully offline zones we recommend CRL snapshots delivered to the proxy on a scheduled basis; the proxy can be configured to import a CRL file and enforce revocation locally.

3) Rotation example (hot-swap)
- We support atomic reloads for the runtime proxy. Sequence: publish new cert -> health-check proxy -> switch listener -> verify client sessions. No full cluster restart required. We recommend a 5–15 minute canary window and automated rollback if health-check fails.

4) Attestation and audit artifacts
- Redwood can provide:
  - Key generation logs (timestamps + host id)
  - KMS/HSM usage logs (if run in-customer-project HSM)
  - Cert rotation events with timestamps
  - Signed statement of custody for a given timeframe (add-on for SOC/ISO audits)

Next steps
- We will: (a) attach the openssl snippets file, (b) prepare a short PoC plan (1–2 hosts) with a canary rotation, and (c) draft the attestation template for your audit team.
- You: confirm tenant vs Redwood-managed preference and whether IP SANs are required.
